2_Introduction: The device achieved a remarkable PCE of 13.95%, with a VOC of 1.0774 V, JSC of 23.483 mA/cm², and FF of 55.1374%. The perovskite precursor solution with a molar concentration of 1.5 mol/L was prepared according to the formula of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2. The perovskite solution was deposited on the substrate by two consecutive spin-coating steps of 1000 rpm for 10 s and 4700 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the spin-coating process, 200 µL of CB was dropped on the perovskite at 8 s, prior to the end of the second procedure. The as-coated film was then annealed at 115 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ formulation inherently leverages A-site cation mixing to enhance phase stability and suppress halide segregation, where the small ionic radius of Cs⁺ (1.81 Å) and larger FA⁺ (2.79 Å) jointly optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.96), mitigating octahedral tilting while reducing Pb–I antibonding character at the conduction band minimum and thus elevating VOC; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.5 mol/L) ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive viscosity-induced aggregation, while the two-step spin-coating regimen—first at 1000 rpm for 10 s to establish uniform wetting and interfacial contact, then ramping to 4700 rpm for 30 s to induce rapid solvent expulsion—synergizes with the timed antisolvent quench (200 µL chlorobenzene at 8 s) to arrest intermediate solvate phases (e.g., δ-FAPbI₃ or PbI₂·DMSO) before irreversible decomposition, thereby promoting direct nucleation of the photoactive α-phase and suppressing residual PbI₂ (as corroborated by the absence of its characteristic XRD peak at ~12.6°, indicating complete conversion and minimal trap-state density at grain boundaries); the subsequent 115 °C/30 min thermal annealing further drives Ostwald ripening, yielding large, oriented grains with low-angle grain boundaries that minimize non-radiative recombination—as evidenced by high and spatially uniform photoluminescence intensity across optical mapping, reflecting homogeneous carrier generation and suppressed trap-assisted recombination, while grayscale intensity analysis confirms >98% film coverage with negligible pinholes, ensuring unbroken charge transport pathways and reduced shunt leakage; collectively, this optimized crystallization pathway yields long carrier lifetimes, low energetic disorder, and balanced electron/hole extraction, culminating in VOC = 1.0774 V, JSC = 23.483 mA/cm², FF = 55.1374%, and PCE = 13.95%.
